title: Formulation of Diblock Polymeric Nanoparticles through Nanoprecipitation Technique
protocol: Dissolve PLGA-carboxylate in solvent at a concentration of 5 mM with gentle stirring.
Dissolve NHS and EDC in the PLGA solution at a concentration of 25 mM each, adding them in a stoichiometric excess of 5 times compared to PLGA.
Stir the PLGA-carboxylate solution containing EDC and NHS gently for about 1 hour to convert it into PLGA-NHS.
Add approximately 10 times volume excess of methanol to precipitate out the PLGA-NHS from the reaction mixture.
Centrifuge the solution at 2000 x g, discard the supernatant, and repeat washing with methanol at least three times.
Dry the PLGA-NHS pellet under vacuum for 30 minutes to remove traces of the washing solution.
Redissolve the PLGA-NHS pellet in the same solvent at a concentration of 5 mM.
Add heterobifunctional PEG (amine-PEG-carboxylate) to the PLGA solution at a concentration of 5 mM, maintaining a stoichiometric ratio of 1:1.
Incubate the mixture solution with constant stirring for 24 hours.
After 24 hours, add methanol in excess to precipitate the PLGA-b-PEG block copolymer out of the reaction mixture.
Repeat washing and centrifugation process three times to remove all excess unreacted PEG.
Dry the PLGA-b-PEG block copolymer under vacuum pressure.
Dissolve PLGA-b-PEG block copolymers in a solvent suitable for the hydrophobic drug or cargo being encapsulated.
Add polymer/drug mixture dropwise to 3-5 volumes of stirring water, achieving a final polymer concentration around 3 mg/mL.
Stir for 2 hours under reduced pressure to allow nanoparticles to form by self-assembly and remove traces of the organic solvent.
Concentrate nanoparticles by centrifugation at 2,700xg for 10 min using an Amicon filter (MWCO 20KDa).
Wash and reconstitute nanoparticles in PBS.
Characterize PLGA-b-PEG using a 400 MHz 1H nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR).
Verify molecular weight of the formed product by Gel permeation chromatography (GPC).
Measure particle size and distribution by dynamic light scattering.
Confirm nanoparticle structure and size distribution with transition electron microscopy (TEM).
Quantify surface zeta potential by ZetaPALS.
Determine drug/cargo loading efficiency using standard HPLC.
Dissolve particles in organic solvent.
Perform HPLC to measure the absorbance of the drug/cargo.
Prepare 30 Slide-A-Lyzer MINI Dialysis units with known fixed quantities of nanoparticles.
Collect content from dialysis unit at fixed time intervals.
Add equal volume of organic solvent to dissolved nanoparticles.
Perform HPLC on samples to quantify drug/cargo content.
